I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. That is what I know best, it suits Quzhou County, and it gives me grain from the same land twice in one year. I do not want to take big risks on crops that need more skill, more market bargaining, or more labor at my age. I will stay with winter wheat already on the land through early summer, then plant summer maize right after harvest so I do not lose time. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care most about stable yield. I will fertilize enough to keep the crop strong but not so much that I waste money, irrigate only at the key growth stages, and spray only when I see real weed, disease, or insect pressure. For wheat, I will focus on water at jointing, booting, and grain filling, and I will watch for aphids, rust, and weeds. After wheat harvest, I will direct-seed maize quickly, keep the seedlings even, topdress nitrogen around the big flare stage, and watch for armyworm, corn borer, and leaf disease. I will manage the land in the simplest reliable way: rotary tillage before wheat, then no-tillage maize after wheat so I save time and moisture.
